name: Morasko meteorite craters
why: Seven small impact craters (largest ~90 m) of a few-thousand-year-old iron meteorite fall: simple bowls with rims, the closest Polish match to small lunar craters.

name: Belchatow open-pit lignite mine
why: A terraced pit ~250 m deep with benches and spoil ridges, a big man-made basin with stepped walls like a large crater.

name: Turow open-pit lignite mine
why: Stepped open pit and overburden dumps at the Polish-Czech-German border: terraced walls and a flat floor.

name: Gora Kamiensk spoil heap
why: A ~200 m high conical heap of mine spoil with regular slopes at the angle of repose, comparable to a lunar cone or dome.

name: Karst dolines, Krakow-Czestochowa Upland
why: Limestone upland with scattered closed depressions (dolines, collapse pits): a pitted surface like lunar pits and small irregular craters.

name: Mining sinkholes near Olkusz / Boleslaw
why: Collapse funnels above old zinc-lead workings in dolomite: steep-walled round pits of tens of metres.

name: Biedrusko military training area
why: Training ground north of Poznan with scattered small pits of a few metres on a sandy plain; pits resemble impact points but are not individually confirmed.

name: Zagan military training area
why: Large forested training ground with a dotted field of small pits in the lidar, consistent with impact points (not individually confirmed).

name: Nowa Deba artillery range
why: Range area with a scatter of small pits and a larger rounded mound on a plain, a low-relief pitted surface.

name: Kettle holes, Suwalki Landscape Park
why: Hummocky moraine with many rounded kettle depressions left by melting dead ice: undulating terrain with irregular closed basins.

name: Sniezne Kotly cirques, Karkonosze
why: Karkonosze slope area at the glacial cirques: long steep smooth slopes of 100s of metres (the cirque shape itself is only partly captured by the 3 km window).

name: Hala Gasienicowa, High Tatra
why: Glacially carved alpine terrain with cirques, tarns and sharp ridges: high relief and steep slopes at 1 m detail.

name: Trzy Korony, Pieniny
why: A limestone massif above the Dunajec gorge with cliffs and steep ridges, the steep rugged end of the comparison.

name: Slowinski mobile dunes, Leba
why: Migrating sand dunes up to ~40 m high: smooth wind-built ridges and slip faces, a Mars-like but lunar-smooth surface.

name: Pustynia Bledowska
why: Inland sand area with low dunes and flat surface: a gentle low-relief plain like lunar mare.

name: Gora Swietej Anny
why: Eroded Neogene basalt volcano with a quarry pit on its flank: a small volcanic cone with a crater-like excavation.

name: Ojcow valley
why: Narrow limestone gorge with cliffs and rock towers: a steep-walled canyon like a lunar sinuous rille at coarse scale.

name: Upper Silesia mining subsidence
why: Industrial area on coal-mined ground: broad flat basins, ponds and embankments (built-up, so partly man-made).
